title: How a model learns what a hammer is, and what the market does around one (MNQ candle vectors)
purpose: Turns every MNQ candle window (16 bars x OHLC) into a 64-number, level-free vector measured in units of the trailing 10-bar mean range R_t (candle_vectors.py:19-32, 124-138). Then asks five things: (1) can a model recognise 7 TA-Lib patterns from the vector alone and does that transfer to 1h/4h, (2) do nearest past windows (k=5/20/50, HNSW) predict direction, (3) what does price do before/after each pattern (path and next-6-candle tests, with day-block bootstrap, placebo and frozen-rule 2021-23 / 2024 / 2025 validation), (4) what shapes do unsupervised autoencoder / VQ / masked-candle models invent, (5) what can chance alone produce. Headline findings printed in prose: recogniser AP on 2025 1m, transfer AUC 0.99-1.00 to 1h/4h, neighbour vote AUC about 0.50 (nearly none clear the null), 1m last-bar-reversal AUC 0.514-0.517, 'Did any pattern carry a tradeable edit into 2025' cell (notebook lines 1479-1487).

text_sections: Title and method note (lines 81-103); S1 formula x = (P - C_t)/R_t with R_t = 10-bar mean range and a live symbol legend; S2 how to read the PCA maps; S3 recogniser method (train 2021-2023, threshold on 2024, score 2025, transfer to 1h/4h) with two measured limits (1m-tuned threshold misses 74% of 1h and 87% of 4h shooting stars; 0.2-0.9% of 1m hammer/harami/doji labels sit on the wrong side of the tick-grid boundary); S4 distance definition and 16-bar thinning; S5 findings: at 1m hammer is followed by a next bar about 0.015 average ranges lower, bullish engulfing 0.01 lower over bars 2-4, bearish engulfing 0.01-0.02 higher over bars 2-11; too small to trade; at 1h nothing clears zero; S6 neighbours know nothing at 1m (AUC 0.50, intervals +/-0.008) while last-bar reversal scores 0.514-0.517; at 1h/4h intervals span 0.13-0.25 so 'nothing detected' means too few firings; S7 HNSW caveat (a WHERE after the index returns k rows gives zero rows: build the table, never filter); S9 unsupervised shape study with the 5-part decomposition (body, upper shadow, lower shadow, close position, gap) and reconstruction loss L, symbol table and data-driven findings; S10 pre-registered design (2021-23 screen with Benjamini-Yekutieli, freeze, 2024 Holm, 2025 once; placebo by trading-day shifts; matched gradient-boosted baseline) with symbol table for Delta_k and net_i. Formula legends (x, Delta_k, net_i) need KaTeX: katex ^0.18.9 is already in package.json.

title: MNQ: every TA-Lib indicator on the candles and what it says about direction
purpose: On front-month MNQ 2025-10-01..2025-12-31 (one roll MNQZ5 to MNQH6 at 2025-12-16), plots candles with overlays, sub-panels and the TA-Lib candlestick patterns, then asks (a) how TA-Lib's 61 pattern rules are built and whether an independent re-implementation agrees, (b) how redundant the ~150 indicators are (correlation matrix, cluster order), (c) whether any indicator predicts the next 1/4/12-bar direction (Spearman IC and AUC-0.5 with block-bootstrap interval, circular-shift permutation null, BH q and a family-wise threshold), (d) whether a walk-forward L2 logistic on every indicator beats base rate / persistence / last-return baselines, (e) whether candlestick patterns work as direction calls, and (f) whether market conditions (prior trend, ADX, RSI, volatility, volume, time of day, session) are consistent when a pattern forms, including the clause-by-clause headroom of each TA-Lib rule and the textbook prior-trend check.

title: The candle vocabulary, and what it is worth
purpose: Reads the stored results of two finished experiments on a Conv1d VQ-VAE codebook of K multi-bar candle archetypes. (1) train_candle_seq.py uses the code symbols as inputs to predict log(forward realized volatility) and scores each representation alone and added to a HAR-RV baseline. (2) train_candle_lm.py asks a masked transformer to predict the next symbol and finds it cannot beat n-gram baselines once symbols stop overlapping. Answers: is the vocabulary worth anything beyond HAR, and what do the archetypes look like.

title: How do you know what to encode?
purpose: Decision procedure for feature selection: an incremental feature ladder on 353,478 MNQ 5-minute bars (fit 2021-2023, scored once on 2025) where each rung adds one named block and must beat a best-of-five shuffled control; four targets. Findings: direction and signed gap are dead; volatility_rate_of_change and volume_conditioned_body earn their place on magnitude targets; the close-to-next-open gap equals the bid-ask spread (2.00 vs 2.04 ticks, ratio 0.981); ladder order does not change conclusions.

title: Fat tails and how many of them the calendar invents (time vs volume vs dollar bars)
purpose: For one futures root and one bar size, shows that the fat tails of calendar-time bar returns shrink when the same 1-minute data is sampled every N contracts (volume clock) or every N dollars (dollar clock) calibrated to the same number of bars, in three panels: WHY (hourly volume varies by orders of magnitude), WHAT (return histogram vs bell curve and observed/predicted count at 1-4 sigma), SO WHAT (every bar beyond k sigma plotted where it happened, by hour and year). Ends with four consequences for Sharpe, triple-barrier labels, position sizing and model fitting.

title: TA-indicator strategy vs 600 MNQ ticks a day (rounds 1-13: model battery, rules, S/R zones, conditional strategies, frequency, seasonality, cascade, zone touches)
purpose: One 1,714-line notebook that is the living lab report for the question 'can TA on one MNQ contract net 600 ticks (150 pts, USD 300) a day after a 5.56-tick round trip'. It reads every table the ta_strategy study (packages/ml-engine/src/ta_strategy) lands, round by round, and answers: what the goal demands (win-rate arithmetic), which configurations/rules/templates came closest, whether multi-timeframe S/R levels and zones hold price better than matched random levels, what time of day/ETH-RTH/calendar does to volatility, whether a 1m->30m swing-break cascade points the way, and what happens at the first touch of a zone. Section 15 is an interactive rebuild of how a zone is built on real candles. Answer so far: 600 is out of reach; best is a few ticks/day of alpha (CLAUDE.md 2026-09-28/29 entries).
text_sections: mo.md blocks to carry over as page copy: (L11-22) title + tick/cost definitions (1 tick=0.25pt=USD0.50; round trip 1.39x2=2.78 USD=5.56 ticks, packages/config/cost_model.json); s1 (L98-113) goal formula net/day = sum_t(g_t - c) = N(pT-(1-p)T-c), p_needed=(G/N+c+T)/(2T), (R+1)T denominator with reward-to-risk R, per-contract goal G/k; s2-3 (L191,233) how to read whiskers/ticks/triangles; s6 (L327) perfect-hindsight zigzag ceiling; s8 (L348) review list ranked by expected ticks/day; s9 (L365-373) conditional TA-Lib rules, 40% win at 2:1 = PF 1.33, net/trade 0.2S-5.56, N>=600/(0.2S-5.56); s10 (L514-533) level families, zones, level quality edge=(held-held_A)-(held_shuf-held_shuf_A), conditional strategies tuned by Optuna on prior years; s11 (L704-708, 736-750) frequency round + 'needed gross per trade = 600/N + c' with legend; s12 (L866-871, 1022-1035) time-of-day study and expected-range formula sqrt(8/pi)*sqrt(pi/2)*L_t*sqrt(sum s_u^2)*P_t; s13 (L1099-1104) cascade definition; s14 (L1291-1299, 1375-1393) zone touch definitions (touch, bounce, next-zone-reach, matched null, lift, Benjamini-Hochberg q=0.10, break-even p*=(S+6.56)/(S+T+1)) and 600-arithmetic trades_needed=600/net; s15 (L1496-1506, 1599-1606) zone construction: single linkage gap>max(w*ATR,4 ticks), strength=distinct families, S=argmax centre<=close, R=argmin centre>close. Every formula already carries a symbol legend (L138-144, 738-745, 1023-1030, 1603-1606) that must be kept and must update with the controls.

title: Volatility value to price range: the exact log-range conversion on MNQ across 1m to 1h
